Q: Nearby locations based on existing database A:

well, you can do this using sql query.

SELECT id, ( 3959 * acos ( cos ( radians(78.3232) ) * cos( radians( lat ) ) * cos( radians( lng ) - radians(65.3234) ) + sin ( radians(78.3232) ) * sin( radians( lat ) ) ) ) AS distance FROM markers HAVING distance < 30 ORDER BY distance LIMIT 0 , 20;

It will find the closest 20 locations that are within a radius of 30 miles to the (78.3232, 65.3234)(latitude, longitude) coordinate (your current location in degree radian). lat, lng are latitude and logitude, database table column names where you store your custom locations (also in degree radian)

To search by kilometers instead of miles, replace 3959 with 6371. refer this question

Q: rsync --copy-unsafe-links problem with a relative symlink (does not copy) A:

[Updated 5/12/26] Jimmix's answer explains what is going on, but there is still a problem with other examples (see below). I agree rsync is doing what the docs say, but now I think the design is flawed: Copied structures can be corrupted by creating invalid symlinks instead of copying files when the links are entirely outside the source tree. For example, given this source:

/tmp/tdir
├── distant
│   ├── file1.txt
│   └── foodir
│       └── link_to_file1.txt -> ../file1.txt
└── src
    └── a
        └── b
            └── link_to_foodir -> /tmp/tdir/distant/foodir

rsync --copy-unsafe-links --links --recursive /tmp/tdir/src/a/ /tmp/tdir/dst/a (note trailing slash on .../src/a/) produces a corrupted result:

/tmp/tdir/dst
└── a
    └── b
        └── link_to_foodir
            └── link_to_file1.txt -> ../file1.txt  # BROKEN LINK

It seems to me rsync should process symlinks to directories in a separate pass, so that symlinks within a linked-to directory are converted into files when necessary (each "pass" would have it's own src & dst tops so the "above the tree" check would mean "above this linked-to subtree" and not above the original root).

The docs say

If you instead copy "/src/subdir/" (with a trailing slash) to "/dest/subdir" that would not allow symlinks to any files outside of "subdir"

...which is true (and blocks security breaches via uplinking), but does not guarantee that the content will be reproduced correctly in the destination. Currently the only work-around is to use --copy-links to prevent all symlinks in the destination, suffering duplicate copies of files in places where symlinks could be preserved.

Q: What messaging and mechanics allows a ServerSocket to move a connection to a dedicated port A:

Nothing gets redirected. A ServerSocket listens on a specific port, accept blocks until a client makes a connection. The ServerSocket's port does not change.

Q: sql statement to fetch data from the database of exactly 5 days past A:

This gets exactly 5 days ago,

SELECT *, DATE_FORMAT(user_registerdate, '%m/%d/%Y') 
FROM ts_user  
WHERE DATE(user_registerdate) = CURDATE() - INTERVAL 5 DAY;

Q: selenium webdriver chrome 116 stopped working A:

This is an issue I had before in VS. I had chromedriver that used to be imported via the package manager. If you used to manage chromedriver via another library, package, or some other custom solution you may need to remove references to that.

It might still be trying to download the wrong version that is no longer available.

Q: connect Jenkins to Microsoft SQL Server? A:

It really depends on what you really want to do. If you just want to run a script which connects to the DB and executes the queries using the command line client, you can use the existing "execute shell / batch" build step, or some of the plugins:

  • ssh plugin - remotely execute a script
  • x-shell plugin - makes it easier to integrate scripts for cross-platform envs

You could also try and build your own starting from the basics, Jenkins library plugins
